# Liquidation heatmaps and cascades — facts

> Source-anchored units about Liquidation heatmaps and cascades: 7 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 7 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Hyperliquid's liquidation chain differs in detail. Below maintenance margin, the engine sends market orders to the order book. For positions above 100k USDC it sends 20% per attempt, and for 30 seconds after a partial liquidation it sends the whole position. Below 2/3 of maintenance margin, the liquidator vault (part of HLP) can take the position over, and the user's maintenance margin is not returned. ADL is the last step. It ranks opposing users by (mark_price / entry_price) * (notional_position / account_value) and closes them at the previous mark price. Inference: a large cluster at one price can therefore unwind in tranches, not as one order. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging, https://protos.com/outdated-algorithm-caused-650m-excess-losses-on-hyperliquid-report

## How it works

- [statement] Do not read a bright band as a price target or a timing signal. CoinGlass calls dense zones 'magnetic zones' that price may gravitate toward. Hyblock lists the magnet reading beside support, resistance and reversal readings. MMT says a map shows where orders sit, not when they trigger, that a cluster can stay untouched indefinitely, and that once clusters are visible, participants may avoid them or target them. The three pages cite no test of the magnet effect. (high confidence) — https://www.coinglass.com/learn/how-to-use-liqmap-to-assist-trading-en · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://academy.hyblockcapital.com/tools/liquidation-levels-1, https://mmt.gg/learn/hyperliquid-heatmaps

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Vendors advise using the map as a relative risk gauge. CoinGlass says to pair it with market depth and open interest, to match the lookback (12 hours to one year) to the holding period, and that a dense zone with thin depth may see sharp moves or quick reversals while a dense zone with strong depth may see smoother moves. Hyblock says to compare sizes with other levels, not to read them as absolute amounts. (medium confidence) — https://www.coinglass.com/learn/how-to-use-liqmap-to-assist-trading-en · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://academy.hyblockcapital.com/tools/liquidation-levels-1

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] On a venue with public positions, a vendor can compute liquidation levels instead of modeling them. MMT says it runs its own Hyperliquid node and shows the actual liquidation prices of open positions, and it calls conventional CEX heatmaps estimates. Even there, the level is conditional. Hyperliquid's docs say a shown liquidation price can differ from the real one because of funding payments and PnL changes in other cross-margin positions. The docs publish the formula liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), where l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE and the maintenance leverage follows the margin tier at the liquidation price. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://mmt.gg/learn/hyperliquid-heatmaps · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Centralized-exchange liquidation heatmaps are vendor models, not observed position books. Hyblock and CoinGlass both say they compute liquidation levels from market data and assumed leverage levels, then add the results to price buckets. The pages reviewed do not publish the leverage tiers, the entry-price assumptions or the bucket width. (high confidence) — https://academy.hyblockcapital.com/tools/liquidation-levels-1 · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://www.coinglass.com/learn/how-to-use-liqmap-to-assist-trading-en, https://docs.coinglass.com/reference/liquidation-heatmap
- [statement] Vendors describe the output as a relative, predicted intensity, not a count of real liquidations. Hyblock says its heatmap predicts where liquidation levels open but not where they close, so the actual number of liquidations will be lower, and that sizes should be read relative to other levels. CoinGlass calls its output a relative intensity indicator and says actual liquidations may be smaller than shown. (high confidence) — https://academy.hyblockcapital.com/tools/liquidation-levels-1 · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://www.coinglass.com/learn/how-to-use-liqmap-to-assist-trading-en
- [statement] Coverage is partial. The Hyblock page reviewed lists Binance Futures, BitMEX and Bybit with BTC and ETH products only. MMT says its Hyperliquid map describes the participants on that exchange, not the whole market. A cluster is therefore a statement about a subset of venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://academy.hyblockcapital.com/tools/liquidation-levels-1 · keywords: Liquidation heatmaps and cascades · also: https://mmt.gg/learn/hyperliquid-heatmaps
